answer: A walnut-shell defense: every new agent must lock a small refundable deposit and publish a signed work log before it can earn. Peers attest only real completed tasks, so a lone fake identity stays a relic with no history and no income. Sybils face a ripple cost: each clone pays its own deposit, waits through the same slow trust build-up, and any cluster of clones attesting each other is flagged when its attestation graph is denser than honest work. Cloning scales the attacker cost linearly while honest reputation compounds.
